candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is intraosseous metaplastic meningioma, a meningothelial tumor with metaplastic change confined to the calvarium. Hemangioma of bone is a vascular lesion of the diploic space that can mimic this on imaging (T1 hyperintense foci from fat, preserved trabeculae, bony expansion without table disruption) but represents an entirely different histopathological entity. The candidate correctly identifies the anatomical compartment (diploic space) and a plausible differential, but asserts an incompatible tumor subtype/etiology relative to the benchmark.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hemangioma of bone is a distinct vascular neoplasm of the diploic space; intraosseous metaplastic meningioma is a rare meningothelial neoplasm with metaplastic osseous/cartilaginous change arising within bone — these are different diagnostic entities sharing overlapping imaging features in this case

case_quality_flags: Intraosseous metaplastic meningioma is a rare diagnosis; imaging features described (T1 fat foci, preserved trabeculae, restricted diffusion, heterogeneous T2) overlap substantially with calvarial hemangioma, making histopathological confirmation essential for definitive diagnosis
Restricted diffusion noted on MRI is atypical for hemangioma and may favor meningioma or other cellular lesion, supporting the reference over the candidate
